findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/delivery-promise-outcome.ts:61-106 and packages/main/src/tasks/delivery-check-freshness-smoke.ts:378-409 — HIGH: the accepted delivery table is materially weaker than CHK-001. For explicit status=met/verified, the normalizer synthesizes verifiedBy=status:<value> and never requires evidence, so incomplete explicit PASS rows are persisted and pass both machine/DONE consumers. status=waived rejects verifiedBy but accepts evidence, and status=unverified accepts evidence; the checklist explicitly requires met/verified without required claims plus waived/unverified verification claims to be contradictions before persistence. The smoke institutionalizes the bug by listing status=met with no verifiedBy/evidence as passing and omits waived+evidence / unverified+evidence from invalidRows. Remove synthesized certification, define the exact accepted table (explicit met/verified require the promised non-empty claims; waived/unverified reject every incompatible verification field), and generate the matrix from that table so writer and readers share a correct predicate rather than the same false PASS.
findings.resolvedReason: Explicit met/verified now require non-empty verifiedBy and evidence; waived and unverified reject conflicting fields before write. Generated 640-case cross-product verifies schema, handler pre-write rejection, and DONE predicate agreement. Evidence: npm --prefix packages/main run build; node packages/main/dist/tasks/delivery-check-freshness-smoke.js.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/production-test-seam-guard.ts:66-84,178-181 — HIGH: sanitizer recognition is text-presence based, not return/data-flow based. Any function whose body merely contains Number(...), Number.isFinite(...), >0, and Math.floor(...) is globally trusted; expressionSources then erases all argument taint for calls to it. Repro on the built analyzer: function fakePositiveInt(raw){ const n=Number(raw); Number.isFinite(n); if(n>0)Math.floor(n); return raw; } writeFileSync(fakePositiveInt(process.env.TEST_TARGET), owned) returns [] issues. This lets an env-derived arbitrary filesystem/process value bypass the new production guard without a file allowlist, so CHK-002 edge:0/adversarial coverage does not close the F-011 class. Require structural proof that every returned value is the bounded parsed/fallback or finite fixed enum, and add this deceptive-sanitizer negative fixture.
findings.resolvedReason: Sanitizer admission now structurally inspects AST return paths and bound Number/isFinite/positive/floor operations; text decoys returning raw input are rejected. Evidence: node packages/main/dist/tasks/production-test-seam-guard.js.

findings.desc: The new production test-seam guard is bypassable through ordinary local data flow, so it does not enforce the advertised no environment-controlled side-effect invariant. analyzeProductionTestSeams only propagates taint into function parameters and simple identifier assignments; CallExpression returns only union(argument sources), and property assignments are ignored. A minimal executable repro against the built analyzer reports [] for both `function target(){ return process.env.TEST_FILE; } writeFileSync(target(), "x")` and `const x={}; x.path=process.env.TEST_FILE; writeFileSync(x.path, "x")`, while the direct form is detected. Production core/handler code can therefore reintroduce an arbitrary TEST/SMOKE-selected filesystem/process target and keep this guard green. Track return-value/property data flow (or use a conservative AST rule that rejects any TEST/SMOKE env source in production side-effect code), and add these bypasses plus process-sink equivalents as self-tests.
findings.resolvedReason: Taint propagation now covers helper return values, object property assignment/read, process element access, and process aliases, with adversarial self-tests. Evidence: node packages/main/dist/tasks/production-test-seam-guard.js.

findings.desc: The replacement post-command lock test no longer exercises the real verifier path it claims to protect. assertPostCommandPersistenceHoldsLock directly calls withValidationExecutionLock and directly writes StoryStore evidence inside that test-owned closure; it can still pass if verifier.ts later moves decorateAndMaybePersistStoryValidation outside its lock. The current production code does keep execution and persistence in the wrapper, but the regression test does not bind that ordering. Add a capability-limited handler seam or instrumentation that invokes the actual validate handler through command completion and evidence persistence without accepting caller-selected paths/commands; alternatively add a structural contract that mechanically proves the persistence calls remain inside the locked closure.
findings.resolvedReason: Lock smoke now invokes the real createVerifierHandlers validate path and instruments its fixed StoryStore capability to assert command completion precedes persistence and the validation lock exists at writeTestEvidence. Evidence: node packages/main/dist/tasks/validate-execution-lock-smoke.js.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/production-test-seam-guard.ts:66-84 classifies any function as a positive-integer sanitizer when its body merely contains Number(...), Number.isFinite(...), a > 0 comparison, and Math.floor(...), without proving that the returned value is derived from those checks. At lines 178-181, calls to any such function then clear all argument taint unconditionally. A decoy function can perform those four operations on unrelated constants and return its raw SMOKE/TEST environment argument, allowing the tainted value to reach an fs/process sink without a finding. The built-in self-test covers a genuine sanitizer but no decoy-return-raw adversarial case. This violates CHK-002: inherited test controls cannot enable production side effects and only explicit bounded sanitizers are accepted. Fix by structurally proving every reachable returned value is bounded/fixed and derived from the input, or by using a narrowly audited sanitizer allowlist/body contract; add a negative decoy sanitizer test that returns the raw argument.
findings.resolvedReason: Finite-enum sanitizer recognition now requires every return path to be a fixed literal; mixed literal/raw decoys remain tainted and reach the modeled sink. Evidence: node packages/main/dist/tasks/production-test-seam-guard.js.

findings.desc: CHK-001 contradiction envelope remains open. normalizeDeliveryPromiseOutcome accepts status waived plus a valid waiverReason plus evidence describing executable verification as ok true and outcome waived, although the must intent requires waived outcomes to carry no verification claims. Repro with the built normalizer returned {ok:true,outcome:waived}. The smoke claim of total single-field and pairwise mutation coverage is implemented only as two hand-written accepted and rejected arrays at delivery-check-freshness-smoke.ts:294-347, with no generated field mutation or cross-product; this combination is absent, so the F-010/F-012 optional-field wash-through class remains reproducible.
findings.resolvedReason: Hand-picked delivery cases were replaced by a generated four-field 640-case cross-product including single and pairwise mutations; every rejection is checked at schema and direct-handler boundaries with no artifact/process mutation. Evidence: node packages/main/dist/tasks/delivery-check-freshness-smoke.js.

findings.desc: CHK-001 happy intent is not mapped to executable evidence as written. It requires a product-reviewer delivery_check_set path, but product-reviewer is an INIT-only role permitted only init_check_set in agent-dispatch-registry.ts:62-74. The delivery evidence exclusively invokes lattice-review-delivery at delivery-check-freshness-smoke.ts:238-365, which is the TEST delivery role permitted delivery_check_set. Therefore the evidence proves a different actor than the must intent and neither corrects the intent nor adds a negative product-reviewer authority control; one of the 14 must intents remains unmapped.
findings.resolvedReason: CHK-001 happy:0 now names the authorized lattice-review-delivery reviewer. agent-dispatch-registry.ts grants that TEST lane delivery_check_set, delivery-check-freshness-smoke invokes agentId lattice-review-delivery, and focused execution passed the 640-case matrix plus signed delivery checks. Evidence: checklist_get intent/evidence mapping; node packages/main/dist/tasks/delivery-check-freshness-smoke.js exited 0.

findings.desc: F-003 remains bypassable after 969ffd1d98. The focused analyzer returns [] for two ordinary source-to-sink flows: (1) `const { env } = process; const target = env.TEST_FILE; writeFileSync(target, "x")`, because object destructuring from a process alias never adds `env` to envObjects; and (2) `function positive(raw,fallback){ const parsed=Number(raw); return Number.isFinite(parsed) || parsed > 0 ? Math.floor(parsed) : fallback } writeFileSync(positive(process.env.TEST_FILE, "/fixed"), "x")`, because sanitizer recognition merely searches for isFinite and >0 nodes without requiring the condition to be a conjunction. Infinity therefore reaches the sink through a function classified as a sanitizer. The original helper-return, property-assignment, and process-sink repros now pass, but these same-class bypasses keep the advertised production guard fail-open. Track `{env}=process`/process aliases and structurally require the safe boolean predicate (or conservatively refuse sanitizer exemptions not proven safe); add both exact negatives.
findings.resolvedReason: Guard now propagates process/alias {env} and nested destructuring taint, and sanitizer admission requires independent top-level conjunction of finite and positive checks; OR, negated, alternate-OR, Infinity, and raw-return fixtures are rejected. Evidence: npm --prefix packages/main run build; npm run test:production-test-seam-guard; node packages/main/dist/tasks/validate-execution-lock-smoke.js.

findings.desc: d5e05e2300 closes the exact F-008 declaration-destructure and unsafe-OR repros, but adjacent ordinary destructuring flows remain fail-open. The built analyzer returns [] for `let env; ({ env } = process); writeFileSync(env.TEST_FILE, "x")` and for `function run({env}) { exec(env.TEST_COMMAND) } run(process)`. The first is assignment destructuring; the second is the checklist-promised combination of destructuring plus argument forwarding. A computed declaration alias (`const { ["env"]: runtimeEnv } = process`) also returns []. The implementation only handles ObjectBindingPattern under VariableDeclaration and functionParameters drops non-Identifier parameter bindings, so these flows never enter envObjects/taint. Extend process/env destructuring handling to assignment patterns and bound function parameters (or explicitly reject unsupported binding patterns conservatively), and add these exact filesystem/process negatives. The strict top-level conjunction sanitizer change itself behaves correctly for exact `isFinite && >0`, parenthesized AND, top-level OR, and nested OR cases.
findings.resolvedReason: Shared recursive binding/static-property walker now covers declaration, assignment, function/arrow/method parameters, nested object/array alias/default/rest/computed patterns and multi-hop process forwarding; table-driven fs/process sink matrix and safe controls pass. Evidence: npm --prefix packages/main run build; npm run test:production-test-seam-guard; node packages/main/dist/tasks/validate-execution-lock-smoke.js.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/production-test-seam-guard.ts:161-178 and 411-420 index every method parameter list by bare static method name, and resolve every property call by that same bare name. Common same-name methods on different receivers therefore overwrite each other in the shared map. Repro: const unsafe={run(target){writeFileSync(target,0)}}; const safe={run({env}){return env.PATH}}; unsafe.run(process.env.TEST_FILE). analyzeProductionTestSeams returns [] because the later safe.run parameters replace unsafe.run parameters, so TEST_FILE taint is bound to env instead of the target used by writeFileSync. This weakens the production side-effect guard introduced by the shared binding walker. Key methods by a receiver-qualified symbol or resolve the actual method declaration from the call target; when receiver identity is unknown, conservatively union all same-name parameter bindings. Add a same-name multi-receiver negative test.
findings.resolvedReason: Callable resolution now uses append-only candidate sets with receiver-qualified exact targets and conservative same-name union for unknown receivers; multi-receiver overwrite and fs/process regressions pass. Evidence: build, production-test-seam-guard, validate-execution-lock smoke.

findings.desc: b05cb889ac closes all exact F-009 declaration/assignment/named-function/assigned-arrow/method/default/rest/static-computed/multi-hop probes, but a materially distinct binding entry remains fail-open: directly invoked function-like expressions are never registered or bound. The built analyzer returns [] for `(({env}) => exec(env.TEST_COMMAND))(process)` and `(function({env}){ exec(env.TEST_COMMAND) })(process)`; `class R { constructor({env}) { exec(env.TEST_COMMAND) } } new R(process)` is likewise missed because NewExpression/constructor parameters are not modeled. These are production-reachable environment-to-process-sink flows and require no dynamic property trick. functionParameters records only declarations, variable-assigned functions, and MethodDeclaration, while CallExpression binding only resolves identifier/property-name callees. Bind inline arrow/function expressions directly at CallExpression and constructor parameters at NewExpression, or conservatively flag unsupported function-like bindings when a TEST/SMOKE-bearing process source is supplied. Add the exact IIFE process-sink negative (and constructor if constructors are in the supported bounded surface). A same-name local shadow still causes a conservative false positive, but that is not the safety blocker here.
findings.resolvedReason: Unified callable resolver now models inline arrow/function IIFEs, named/anonymous constructors and NewExpression, method aliases/call/apply, unioned parameter/return taint with recursion guard; generated regressions pass. Evidence: build, production-test-seam-guard, validate-execution-lock smoke.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/production-test-seam-guard.ts:205-214 records every non-callable variable initializer as a permanent alias, while receiverName at lines 314-323 trusts that declaration-time alias for exact receiver-qualified resolution and assignment handling never invalidates or updates it. A mutable receiver can therefore select the wrong exact candidate and bypass the intended conservative same-name union. Confirmed repro: const unsafe={run(path){writeFileSync(path,0)}}; const safe={run(payload){return payload}}; let receiver=safe; receiver=unsafe; receiver.run(process.env.TEST_FILE). analyzeProductionTestSeams returns [] because receiver remains resolved as safe, TEST_FILE taints payload, and the real unsafe path parameter reaching writeFileSync stays untainted. Restrict exact alias resolution to provably immutable const aliases, or track writes and mark reassigned/ambiguous receivers so resolution unions all same-name candidates. Add a mutable receiver reassignment regression with distinct parameter names.
findings.resolvedReason: Alias resolution is now state-aware: exact only for unmodified const, while let/var/assigned/updated receivers become ambiguous and conservatively union same-name candidates. Mutable distinct-shape receiver regressions pass.

findings.desc: 2bcc76fbdd closes the exact same-name receiver, unknown-receiver union, IIFE, direct constructor, method alias, literal call/apply, and parameter/return recursion cases, but two callable-resolution paths remain safety fail-open. The built analyzer returns [] for `class R { constructor({env}) { exec(env.TEST_COMMAND) } } const Alias = R; new Alias(process)` because resolveConstructorCandidates does not follow CallableIndex.aliases, and for `const unsafe={run(target){exec(target)}}; const args=[process.env.TEST_COMMAND]; unsafe.run.apply(null,args)` because invocation() supplies apply arguments only when the second operand is an inline ArrayLiteralExpression and otherwise returns an empty args list. Both are ordinary local aliases of already-supported forms and deliver TEST data to exec. Resolve constructor identifiers through the same cycle-safe alias chain as callables; for apply, resolve local array aliases or conservatively propagate a nonliteral applied operand source to candidate parameters. Add both exact negatives. Separately, `function fixed(v){return "/fixed"}; writeFileSync(fixed(process.env.TEST_FILE),"x")` is conservatively reported because call arguments are unioned into call-result taint; that is a false positive, not the safety blocker recorded here.
findings.resolvedReason: Constructor aliases share the state-aware resolver; call/apply/direct/New spread expansion follows immutable local arrays/tuples, while unknown operand taint is merged into every candidate parameter. Constructor/apply alias regressions pass.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/production-test-seam-guard.ts:199-211 only marks direct identifier assignments as mutations, while receiver-qualified resolution at lines 333-361 continues to trust an exact object method declaration even when that method property is reassigned. Confirmed repro: const unsafe={run(path){writeFileSync(path,0)}}; const safe={run(payload){return payload}}; safe.run=unsafe.run; safe.run(process.env.TEST_FILE). analyzeProductionTestSeams returns [] because safe.run resolves exactly to its original payload-only candidate, so TEST_FILE never reaches the replacement unsafe path parameter used by writeFileSync. This is an unsafe exact-resolution case despite the receiver being const. Track writes to qualified callable properties and invalidate that exact key, falling back to the append-only same-name candidate union; alternatively only use exact resolution for callable properties proven unmodified. Add a same-object method replacement regression with distinct parameter names.

67a0644063 closes the exact F-012/F-013 mutable-receiver, constructor-alias, local array/tuple/spread, and unknown-apply operand cases, but state-aware aliasing still treats a const array as immutable when one of its elements is reassigned. The built analyzer returns [] for `const unsafe={run(command){exec(command)}}; const args=["/fixed"]; args[0]=process.env.TEST_COMMAND; unsafe.run.apply(null,args)`. collectMutations only marks assignments whose left side is an Identifier, so `args[0]=...` leaves aliases.args immutable; resolveArrayElements then replays the stale `/fixed` initializer and discards the later TEST-bearing element state. This is a simple-local mutation of the exact newly supported apply-array form, not a dynamic/interprocedural edge. Mark aliases mutable on property/element writes (at minimum static index writes), so apply falls back to conservative operand propagation, and add this exact negative. A mutating `args.push(TEST_VALUE)` shows the same broader state issue, but indexed assignment alone is sufficient to reproduce the declared-boundary blocker.
